correctness.rationale: The source’s scalar reduction is exact. For every \(I>0\), direct differentiation gives strictly positive partial derivatives of \(F\) with respect to \(\beta_1\) and \(\beta_2\). At \(\beta_1=\beta_1^\ast\), \(\beta_2=\beta_2^\ast\), clearing positive denominators gives \(-I^2(C_0+C_1I)\) times a positive factor, with \(C_0>0\) and \(C_1>0\) because \(H>0\), \(P>0\), \(M-\mu=\alpha\sigma>0\), and \(M-A\sigma=\mu(1-\sigma)\ge0\). Hence the scalar function is negative for every positive \(I\) at the extremal corner and therefore throughout the claimed rectangle. The proof is universal, not experimental; exact-rational replay only checks algebraic consistency.

value.rationale: The source highlights the no-subcritical-endemic-equilibrium statement as Numerical Finding 7.1, so converting it into an exact theorem closes a stated mathematical gap rather than adding a routine parameter example. The result also sharpens the interpretation of \(\beta_2^\ast\): it is not merely a local bifurcation-direction threshold but an exact global exclusion boundary for positive equilibria throughout \(R_0\le1\). This distinction is directly relevant to how the source organizes eradication and bistability regimes, while the claim deliberately leaves global trajectory convergence open.
